To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

clustering of NMDA receptors containing GluN1/GluN2A subunits is mainly mediated by their C-terminal domain and the association of this subunit with PSD-95, and that this clustering is important in the synaptic localization of GluN1/ GluN2 A-containing NMDA receptors.
the C-termini of the GluD2 and GluN2 proteins are involved in the surface clustering of NMDA receptor subunits in cultured rat hippocampus neurons.

clustering of NMDARs on the surface of cultured hippocampal neurons is mainly mediated by GluN2C-terminal domain of GluN1/GluN2A receptors and that this process may involve the interaction of GluN 2A with PSD-95.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the surface distribution of NMDARs with different GluN subunits in the hippocampus.
a novel mechanism of the synaptic localization of NMDARs.
the distribution patterns of surface NMDAR subunits in cultured rat hippocampus neurons, and the underlying molecular mechanisms of the distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clustering of surface NMDAR subunits in cultured rat hippocampus neurons is mainly mediated by C-terminus GluN2a.
the C-termini of GluN1 and GluN2 are important determinants of the clustering and synaptic distribution of NMDARs, and this is a novel mechanism underlying the functional diversity of NMDAR subtypes.
clustering distribution of surface NMDAR subtypes is mainly mediated by their carboxyl terminus, and the GluN1 C-terminal domain also contributes to this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-termini of GluN1 and GluN2 play different roles in NMDAR clustering, and the C-terminin of GluN3A may also play a role.
the clustering distribution patterns of NMDARs are determined by the C-terms of the Glu subunits, and this may be a mechanism for the subunit-specific functions of NMDAR.
the clustering of GluN subunits is not only dependent on the N-termini but also on the C-termini.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GluN1/GluN2A complex is more inclined to form clusters on the cell surface than GluN1/ GluN2 complexes, which may be related to the fact that NMDARs with GluN2As are more involved in synaptic transmission and long-term synaptic plasticity.
the GluN C-terminus is a key determinant of NMDAR surface distribution and synaptic location, and this may contribute to the functional diversity of NMDAR subtypes.
the GluN subunit composition of NMDARs can affect the surface distribution of these receptors.
